localLife.nature: West Hills is one of the newer parts of the Valley — most of it built out after the 1980s — which shows in wider streets, more uniform tract layouts, and a quieter, more master-planned feel than the older, denser blocks toward the eastern Valley.
localLife.community: Families drawn to newer construction and a quieter, more suburban pace than Woodland Hills' office corridor next door, with easy access to the open space along the Upper Las Virgenes edge.
localLife.howWeHelp: We service the more standardized systems that came with West Hills' newer, master-planned construction, and we know the far-west Valley's heat doesn't care that this end of town is quieter than the rest.

seasonalNotes.focus: Far-west Valley summers run just as hot as anywhere else in the Valley — newer construction here doesn't mean newer equipment, since a lot of original-installation systems from the 1980s and 90s are still in service.
A fall check on a West Hills home built in the original development wave often reveals equipment that's original to the house — worth knowing before, not during, a summer-to-winter transition.
